column1: # THE CAMPAIGN DAY, machine-readable. The spine of campaign/calendar.md.
# Append-only. One row per in-game day or span that got played. The CURRENT DAY
# is max(day) -- derived, never stored, so it cannot drift.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: the day count was kept in the DM's head and drifted until
# the player caught it on Torsat's illness. `calendar.md` was then made
# authoritative -- but it is prose, so "what day is it" was still a reading
# rather than a query, and it is the single most frequently needed fact in the
# campaign. See dlwork/tooling_plan.md, the demand-side table.
# calendar.md remains the NARRATIVE record and is much richer than this. This
# file carries only what a tool needs: the number, where the party was, and one
# line to recognise the day by.
# Seeded 2026-09-11 from calendar.md. Days 1-76 are summarised in spans where
# calendar.md itself does; the day NUMBERS are the load-bearing part.

column4: summary
Expedition 1. Into the caves.
Slept in area 5. Emerged about 11 p.m.
Torsat's rash and fever. Salvage sold, 170 gp. Surety before Ottir. Halm's mule in restitution.
The patrol begins. Osk met on the road.
Torsat clear. Wend still refusing.
Torsat fully fit.
WEND COMES ROUND, before anyone spoke. Coll's standing instruction given.
Outbound. The cold camp thirty yards off the road, four people, a fortnight old.
Nan and her two children walk in. Two men off Ellery's.
The party's first mule.
Two carts bought, 50 gp each. Dragon scales sold, 110 gp.
Wend's open-handed-where-it-is-finite rule adopted: iron and salt at cost, price visible.
THE CLIP SOLD. 1,200 gp. Rosewood 350 besides.
The Ludbury spend, 1,038 gp. Fenn paid at his gate.
Ede wants a month to shut up her cottage.
THE ARTICLES BEGUN. Ancel on the road, 11 -> 81. Wend takes the factorship.
WEND AND ANCEL, 127. Four buyers named; a penny in the pound for three years. Six unlisted hands to Marrow's on a written right of return.
Marrow paid in the square. Gyll pays restitution to the eleven, aloud, Ottir witnessing.
Market day. ~178 gp of small goods moved.
HASK, DELLIE AND ISTA BECOME 1st-LEVEL CHARACTERS. Art. 7 agreed: 8 gp the tod, cap 500.
Check-ins. Halm's standing want, unmet: "what I'd want is a RUN."
Perrin, usher of the hall, met riding north. 92, then 98.
Market day. Ottir's hearing.
EXPEDITION 7 SETS OUT. Nine underground for the first time.
The skeletons behind the secret door into area 9.
Wend: only half the small goods have sold.
CUDDY'S ANSWER ON THE CRAG. Holy water refused. The dwarf in irons told. Licence counselled.
THE PETITION. Licence granted and backdated.
Ottir and Yrtone ride home. The party is now a known quantity in Sir Aymer's country.
Toller finds the same hole Wend found. THE LETTER TO WACE, and the receipt trick.
South with Halm's cart. Wat rides for Draycot.
Marchford at dusk. Pell the carrier met: "Ludbury. That's the whole mystery."
THE VIAL IS NAMED: REALGAR. Father Doule is 5th level and Marchford has no font. The small-goods line closes, 573 on 357.
Lyde's terms met. 31 gp paid at his door; 18 owing in three quarters.
WACE'S RECEIPT ARRIVES. Toller pays ~250. Over a thousand gold for the first time. Wend turns the narrow loom round.
Expedition 8 outfitting. Six ropes, eight person-weeks standard rations.
EXPEDITION 8. The barrel re-coopered behind a spiked door.
Areas 8 and 9 stripped. One troglodyte on the loaded walk out.
HOME. The barrel sold to Holt, 58 gp. Wend's week of writing done a day early.
THE STRUCTURE SIGNED, art. 13. Nan can grade wool. The wool operation formed.
THE DWARF TO DRAYCOT. Hask leaves with the wool party.
Cuddy frail. A MAN HAS BEEN SENT ABOUT THE ANIMATED DEAD. Dellie taught the words. Home that evening.
Ottir on the chapel roof. Wend has no amounts. THE CARRIAGE GAP: "at cost" was ~60 gp below cost.
EXPEDITION 9 SETS OUT. Eight walk north at first light -- Hask is on the wool road and Rowe went with Halm. Night at Coll's basecamp.

IN. *** NEW STANDING FORMATION FOR EXPEDITION 9: rank 1 YRTONE (shield, sling) / DAVE (shield, sword) / TORSAT (BOW); rank 2 FRYTHON (darts) / TRISTLE (bow) / ISTA (lantern, darts); rank 3 DELLIE (shield, sling) / BLARTHO (shield, sling). *** Thirteen squares to the alcove at (17,13).

EXPEDITION 9 ENDS. Out at midday, past the empty basecamp without stopping, on the north road by one. ~13 miles before dark, camped on the road; into Wethersby mid-morning. TWO TROGLODYTES at (24,37) cost TORSAT A WEEK -- first character in the campaign to serve the DMG p.82 week under RAW, the house rule having been retired the same day. 94 xp. No treasure. A door in a bay off the y=35 corridor still unopened

EXPEDITION 10 GOES IN, two days after expedition 9 came out. SEVEN -- Torsat invalid at the Inn to day 87, Hask still on the wool road. *** FORMATION: rank 1 YRTONE (sling, shield) / DAVE (sword, shield) -- TWO MEN IN A CORRIDOR THAT FITS THREE; rank 2 FRYTHON (darts) / ISTA (lantern, darts) / TRISTLE (BOW, not the spear); rank 3 BLARTHO (sling, shield) / DELLIE (sling, shield). *** They came back for one thing: the plain iron-banded door in the bay off the y=35 corridor, walked past twice on day 79 without anybody listening at it

EXPEDITION 10 OUT at 11h06m under, the party's second-longest. Half an hour down the unmade outcrop in the dark to Coll's empty camp, and slept there. ALL SEVEN WALKED OUT. Dellie serving DMG p.82 until about day 88 -- the SECOND character in three days after Torsat. Taken: 36 arrows, a bronze statuette, 29 cp. Mapped: the whole north-east quarter, proved to be ONE CLOSED CIRCUIT hanging off the y=35 corridor, with B1's own confusion maze screening the middle of it

HOME. Left Coll's camp at first light, half an hour to the road and twenty miles south. Arrived in the evening. DELLIE INVALID to ~day 88, TORSAT to 87 -- two of nine out of action at once, for the first time in the campaign. *** THE WOOL PARTY IS DUE TODAY *** -- Hask, Nan, Tam, Halm, Rowe -- and Osk got back to Wethersby on the 81st, so Wend has already had him

CORRECTION to the row above, appended not rewritten. THE TIMELINE IS: out of the dungeon at round 666 on the 81st, about five in the evening; half an hour down the outcrop to Coll's camp; SLEPT THERE the night of the 81st-82nd; left at FIRST LIGHT ON THE 82nd and walked the twenty miles, ARRIVING WETHERSBY THE EVENING OF THE 82nd -- one day, as rules/overland.md says a laden march makes, and as day 46-47 attests with an invalid in the party. THE 83rd IS THE DAY AFTER: the wool party's due date, with the morning free before they come in

*** THE PARTY SPLITS. *** SOUTH WITH THE CARAVAN (5): Yrtone, Tristle, Ista, Blartho, Hask -- three carts, Wend's list as freight and THE FORTY JARS as the party's own cargo, with TAM representing Wend and doing her buying. Ista teaches the camp cooking and the work is shared. EAST AND SOUTH BY HORSE (2): DAVE AND FRYTHON on the party's two LIGHT riding horses, 60 miles a day, ON ROADS THE WHOLE WAY -- Marchford, Ludbury, then three days east to WRAYE for the library, the unidentified ring (L029) and a correspondent for Toller. Torsat (to 87) and Dellie (to ~88) at the Inn

THE RIDERS EAST: Dave and Frython out of Ludbury at first light on the 87th, three days east to WRAYE on good road, carrying NEOT'S PEARL and the unidentified ring. THE CARAVAN reaches Marchford the same day -- Yrtone, Tristle, Ista, Blartho, Hask and TAM, with Wend's list and the forty jars for Trebb. The two halves are now four days apart and cannot send word; the rendezvous is WETHERSBY

THE RIDERS TURN FOR HOME. Wraye at first light on the 90th, 200 miles by road -- Wraye to Ludbury 75, Ludbury to Marchford 50, Marchford to Wethersby 75 -- about three and a third days on light horses. *** THE ROAD HOME RUNS THROUGH LUDBURY AND NEOT IS IN IT, AND THERE IS NOTHING TO TELL HIM YET *** because the ring stays unread until Wethersby. FRYTHON'S BOOK NOW: shocking grasp, read magic, sleep, IDENTIFY, ENLARGE/REDUCE -- 5 of a maximum 14 against a minimum of 8. CHARM PERSON CLOSED FOREVER at INT 17 (L049)

THE RIDERS PASS THROUGH MARCHFORD and do not stop for business -- Trebb had the forty jars off Yrtone on the 87th and there is nothing here for two men in a hurry. Out of Ludbury about midday on the 91st after Neot, ~30 miles before dark; a full 60 on the 92nd, which puts them 40 miles NORTH of Marchford by nightfall. *** THE CARAVAN IS ALREADY AHEAD OF THEM: *** Yrtone, Tristle, Ista, Blartho, Hask and Tam left Fenn's on the 88th, 100 miles by cart at 25 a day = four days, HOME ON THE 92nd. The two halves have been four days apart and unable to send word since the 84th and they miss each other on the road by one day

*** THE PARTY IS WHOLE AGAIN. *** Dave and Frython ride in mid-afternoon on the 93rd -- 125 miles Ludbury to Wethersby at 60 a day on LIGHT horses (rules/overland.md, DMG p.58), the caravan a day before them. NINE DAYS OUT, and the riders covered roughly 400 miles of it. WHAT THEY BRING BACK: enlarge/reduce and identify copied into Frython's book (5 spells of a max 14); charm person closed forever at INT 17 (L049); NEOT'S PEARL RETURNED UNSPENT because identify's window on the ring shut weeks ago; and ORDRIC, A SAGE AT WRAYE -- a name and a town and nothing else. THE RING IS STILL UNREAD. Torsat came off invalid on the 87th and Dellie about the 88th, so for the first time since day 83 ALL NINE ARE FIT

*** EXPEDITION 11 SETS OUT. NINE WALK NORTH -- the first time the whole party has gone underground together since day 45. *** Hask asked and free: Wend has the board to put up, four letters out to holders (L043), Bern waiting on a cloth decision and Fenn now hers entirely, but NONE OF IT IS HASK'S THIS WEEK (d6=1) -- he is her holder man, that work is done until the post comes back, and he would rather go down a hole than sit in town while letters travel. Out of Wethersby at first light, twenty miles to the crag turning, UNEVENTFUL ROAD (d6=5). Night at Coll's basecamp, empty as it always is -- which is the point of it. CARRIED: 11 person-weeks of food (8.5 standard + 2.5 iron = 77 person-days = 8.5 days for nine, and the iron half of that is an ESTIMATE the repo flags); 474 turns of light -- 15 sealed flasks, 1 broached, 8 torches, 52 turns in three lamps; 13 iron spikes with 9 still emplaced below; 7 sound ropes. NO OBJECTIVE DECLARED AND NONE ASKED FOR -- the party explores, and formation is given at the cave mouth, not in town

EXPEDITION 11 ENDS AT COLL'S BASECAMP. Out of the crag at round 854 on the evening of the 95th -- FOURTEEN HOURS FOURTEEN MINUTES, the longest ever by 54 minutes, and THE FIRST EXPEDITION OF ANY LENGTH WITH NO DAMAGE TAKEN BY ANYBODY. Half an hour down the unmade outcrop with 421 lb of salvage, made possible by ELEVEN carriers: BRAND and ORM came down with them. Night at the empty camp, Ista cooking for eleven, and nothing for Yrtone or Blartho to dress. Twenty miles south to Wethersby in the morning

*** THE SALVAGE DOES NOT COME. *** At first light in steady rain the party read its own encumbrance and stopped: 421 lb over eleven backs is 38 lb a head BEFORE mail and shield, which is the DMG p.58 HEAVY band -- ten miles a day, not twenty, so twenty-one miles to Wethersby becomes two days and a night in the open on 17.5 person-days of rations for eleven mouths. THEY STACKED IT ALL UNDER THE LEAN-TO INSTEAD and walked out light. Coll's trail is cart-passable to that flat and the carts are in Wethersby; they are coming back for it. Casters took the same loadouts they have carried all expedition. Out at first light, twenty-one miles down the north road in the wet, INTO WETHERSBY AT DUSK -- eleven of them, Brand and Orm included, and not one thing on the road all day.
MORNING: the buying, and MUND THE SMITH met for the first time in 96 days. AFTERNOON: north with two carts, three horses and twelve people.

*** NORTH WITH TWO CARTS, THREE HORSES AND TWELVE PEOPLE -- AND THEY ARRIVE IN THE DARK. *** The morning went on the buying: 51 gp of goods, MUND THE SMITH met for the first time in 96 days (reaction 52, neutral, he had 200 spikes and 20 lb of nails out of stock and said nothing about where his bar came from), and TWO FLASKS OF OIL because two is every flask in Wethersby. Eight person-weeks of rations was all the town could reach -- early spring, the hungry gap, 240 lb of food asked for in one morning off-market, two weeks at the PHB price and six at half over. *** THE COST OF SHOPPING FIRST IS DAYLIGHT: *** loaded and rolling by late morning, and a cart makes 25 miles in a day, so 21 miles ran out of light about two short of the crag turning. Up Coll's graded trail by lamp, into the empty basecamp somewhere near eight. NOTHING ON THE ROAD ALL DAY (d6=1) -- with 200 spikes, 20 lb of nails, 160 lb of food and three horses in the open, which is the load DESPERATE MEN came out for on the day-60 leg. Rain easing to grey and damp (d6=3). 454 lb of stores is 28 percent of ONE cart; the 421 lb of salvage still under the lean-to makes 82 percent of one between them, and there are two.
EXPEDITION 12. Eleven in, Rowe minding the camp. (23,22), then area 34's spikes, then the kitchen.

*** EXPEDITION 12: TWO HOURS AND ONE MINUTE, THE SHORTEST IN THE CAMPAIGN, AND THE SECOND CLEAN ONE RUNNING. *** In at dawn, out at round 121, nobody scratched, no monster seen, no door forced, no spike driven. A TOOL TRIP: they went in for one object and came out with three. CARRIED OUT: the large cast-iron kettle with 20 ft of riveted chain (180 lb) on a TWO-POLE SEDAN RIG the player designed -- a pole on each shoulder, front man and back man -- plus 13 pots and pans (10 sound, 3 holed and taken for scrap) and THE IRON SHEAVE BLOCK off the kitchen ceiling, which exists in the load only because the player asked why the hacksaws were supposedly in a cart. ~270 lb. FIVE WANDERING CHECKS INCLUDING THE FIRST clock.py extra IN CAMPAIGN HISTORY, bought by forty minutes of sawing iron -- ALL FIVE EMPTY. Then half an hour of unmade outcrop with 180 lb on poles: d6=4, slow and ugly with frequent rests and nothing broken and nobody hurt. Rowe had the camp and the animals the whole time. Day 99: twenty-one miles south to Wethersby with two carts and about 690 lb.

*** TIME-OF-DAY CORRECTION, player-caught: THE DM WROTE 'EVENING OF THE 98th' AND IT IS LATE MORNING. *** In at first light, 121 rounds under = TWO HOURS ONE MINUTE, then about an hour down the outcrop because of the kettle. That puts them back at the basecamp somewhere around TEN OR ELEVEN IN THE MORNING with the whole day in front of them, which is the entire reason the next thing is possible at all. The DM defaulted to 'evening' because every previous expedition has been eight to fourteen hours long and ended at dusk; a two-hour trip is a new shape and the habit wrote the wrong sentence. AND TORSAT IS 6/6 -- see hp_log, the first natural-healing row in the campaign. *** WHAT THE SPARE DAY BUYS: the party sets out to FIND THE DRY WATERCOURSE, the L053 rendezvous nobody has ever laid eyes on, three days before they must be standing in it with 37 gp. Rowe stays with the mules, the carts and 690 lb; the THREE HORSES go, LED not ridden, because a led horse is the cheapest possible test of whether a cart can follow.

*** THE WATERCOURSE IS FOUND, AND THREE THINGS CAME WITH IT. *** Out about eleven with the three horses on the lead, Rowe keeping the camp, Brand and Orm gone up the outcrop with three torches and the party's whole briefing. Two miles north-east round the foot of the crag, no trail, and FOUND LATE (d6=2) with little daylight left to look about. (1) THE BEARING WAS EXACT. Round the north shoulder, east then north along the foot of the scree, up it to an overhang with a slab, and the mouth below where a cart can stand -- Durnhak described it to a man who wrote it down and every word of it holds. (2) A GAME TRAIL (d6=6 for recent sign, d6=2 for what, d6=5 on how well they can read it): FERAL GOATS working down the scree daily, sign hours old, and IT IS WHY THE GROUND IS CROSSABLE AT ALL -- the beaten line along the foot is theirs. Ninety-eight days and nobody has seen them because the party has only ever gone up the SOUTH-WEST outcrop and straight into the hole. *** THERE IS MEAT ON THIS HILL AND ELEVEN PEOPLE ON FOUR AND A HALF DAYS OF RATIONS. *** (3) AND THE PLAYER'S HOPED-FOR LOOP IS HALF REAL (d6=4): from the mouth there is OPEN GROUND RUNNING WEST toward the north road -- rough, unmade, but better going than the scree they came by. Three and a half miles of it, and it meets the road NORTH OF THE CRAG TURNING, which is the outer limit of everything the party has ever walked. No time to scout it today.

*** TIMELINE CORRECTION, PLAYER-CAUGHT: 'If we took 2 hours to go those 2 miles, which would be very, very slow, we would be there at 1 PM.' HE IS RIGHT AND THE DM CONFUSED A DAILY RATE WITH AN HOURLY PACE. *** rules/overland.md's 'off the road, 10 mi/day' is a FULL MARCHING DAY figure -- it already carries rests, obstacles, watering and the fact that nobody walks ten hours at a constant pace. Dividing it by ten to get 1 mi/hour and then rounding DOWN to 0.8 for a two-mile leg is the same error as costing a sprint at a marathon's pace. On a beaten goat trail, leading horses, over rough but crossable ground, 1.5 mi/hour is honest and generous-slow. *** SO THE TWO MILES IS AN HOUR AND A HALF, NOT TWO AND A HALF, AND THEY REACH THE NORTH FOOT ABOUT HALF PAST TWELVE. *** WHAT THE d6=2 'FOUND LATE' ACTUALLY BOUGHT, now that the walk is costed properly: it is not the WALKING that took the afternoon, it is THE LOOKING. The foot of that crag is cut by several gullies and blind clefts and only one of them is a dry watercourse with an overhang and a slab above it; they worked up and down the line checking them for about three hours. FOUND AROUND FOUR, roughly an hour and a half of light left in early spring, away by half past, back at the camp near dusk. The party was never short of daylight for the WALK -- it was short of daylight for the SEARCH, which is a different thing and the dice said so.

*** THE PARTY SPLIT AND BOTH HALVES GOT HOME. *** SIX WALKED the two miles of goat-line back round the north foot -- Torsat, Tristle, Frython, Blartho, Dellie, Ista -- in about an hour and twenty, home before full dark. THREE RODE THE LOOP AND MAPPED IT: 3.7 miles of open waste south-west from the watercourse mouth to the ROAD'S END, 1 mile of fraying road south to the crag turning, 1.8 miles up Coll's trail. *** 6.5 MILES AGAINST THE WALKERS' 2, about two and a quarter hours, the unwalked part done in the last of the light and the known part in the dark. *** THE PRIZE WAS NOT THE ROUTE. It was finding that THE NORTH ROAD ENDS A MILE ABOVE THE CRAG TURNING (d6=2) -- and that is why a stronghold forty years empty sat unlooted a day's walk from a market town. ON THE CART QUESTION: the waste is better going per mile and nearly twice as far, so NEITHER approach is plainly right for the 101st and the party now owns that choice instead of guessing it. Three new places and three new ways on the map, all of them KNOWN and none of them hearsay. Eleven at the camp by dark, nobody hurt, and BRAND AND ORM CAME OUT OF THE CRAG WHOLE.

*** THE PARTY SPLITS SOUTH AND NORTH. *** NIGHT OF THE 98th: Brand volunteered at the fire that they had found the smithy cache, dug the ash off, taken nothing and covered it back -- before anybody had been near the place, and it is the answer to the d6=5 'something with hands' that the party would otherwise have found on the 99th and had to wonder about. THE GOATS CAME DOWN IN THE DARK (d6=5, then d6=2) and away again, sign at dawn only -- AND THE REASON IS SITTING IN places.tsv: COLL'S CREW BUILT A BOXED SPRING ON THIS FLAT. The goats come to the water. The party does not have to go up the scree to find them; they come to the camp. MORNING OF THE 99th, grey and damp, no rain (d6=3): HASK AND DELLIE SOUTH with one cart, one mule, 421 lb of salvage plus pans, block and kettle -- 21 miles, Wethersby by evening, MARKET ON THE 100th, Wend to be asked about the kettle first, Sarn to be borrowed off Coll if he can be spared. AND SEVEN GO BACK INTO THE CRAG -- Dave, Torsat, Tristle, Frython, Yrtone, Blartho, Ista -- for the smithy depot: 8 torches, 13 iron spikes and EIGHT AND A HALF PERSON-WEEKS OF FOOD, which is 59 person-days lying under cold ash 940 ft inside the door while the party rations itself at the camp. Rowe keeps the beasts. Brand and Orm ask to come along (d6=5) and ask something with it.

*** EXPEDITION 13 IS OUT, ALIVE, AT ROUND 358 -- 358 rounds under, just under six hours. TWO FIGHTS AND THE PARTY WAS TOUCHED ONCE, BY ITS OWN ARROW. *** IN: eight. Dave, Yrtone, Torsat, Tristle, Frython, Ista, Blartho and BRAND, who took his first action in a fight and who got a stat line the same hour (0 level, AC 10, 3 hp, MM p.66). Rowe minded the camp; Hask and Dellie away. *** DONE: the smithy depot lifted; three orc encounters PARLEYED rather than fought; DURNHAK MET FACE TO FACE and four spikes handed over early; one GNOLL killed at a break-off without touching anybody; the HALF-ELLIPSE CORRIDOR round area 12 walked and mapped, a curve the grid had been reporting as a T-junction; AREA 12 THE LIBRARY entered, four orc squatters killed inside a single surprise segment, and the room searched out. *** CARRIED OUT: a silver mirror (module valuation 90 gp), ten books, three scrolls, 31 ep and 5 gp in coin, and a morning star and a gnoll-sized sword as salvage iron. *** XP TAKEN ON THE WAY OUT: 54 gnoll, 54 orcs, 20 coin. The mirror, the books and the scrolls pay when they sell. *** SPENT: one cure light wounds for a single point, 8.6 turns of lamp oil, and nothing else -- four spikes went into the library doors and all four came back out.

*** DAVE AND TRISTLE RODE SOUTH THE SAME AFTERNOON THEY CAME OUT OF THE CRAG. *** Out of the dungeon just after midday, down the outcrop, and on the road by early afternoon with all three horses -- two ridden, the third packed with ten books, three scrolls and the copper wire. 131 lb against a riding horse's 300 at normal move, so no penalty and no slower pace. 1.8 miles up Coll's trail to the crag turning, then TWENTY MILES OF MADE ROAD south: DMG p.58 gives a rider 40 a day on a medium mount, so half a day, four or five hours. Into Wethersby about dusk. *** THE REST OF THE PARTY STAYS AT THE BASECAMP with Rowe, the two carts and the mules. The 101st is the watercourse and THE PLAYER HAS NAMED THE ROUTE: the long way round -- Coll's trail down, the fraying road, then the open waste from the road's end -- 6.5 miles rather than the two trackless ones round the north foot, and from FIRST LIGHT.

*** INTO WETHERSBY AT DUSK, AND TOLLER'S SHOP IS SHUT. d6=2, rolled before the scene. *** He is a one-man dealer and the night before market is when he lays out a stall or goes to bed early for it. Dark window, locked door, nobody in. *** THE TOWN IS FILLING FOR MARKET DAY: carts in the square that were not there on the 97th, the inn loud, strangers off the southern road. Hask and Dellie are somewhere in it. *** THE HORSES NEED STABLING AND THE 131 LB OF BOOKS NEEDS PUTTING SOMEWHERE, and the player has already said what to do if Toller will not have them -- 'store it somewhere safe'. Not decided for him.

*** DAY 100. MARKET DAY IN WETHERSBY, and the party's own weekly count makes it one -- the 37th was a market and it has run every seventh day since: 37, 44, 51, 58, 65, 72, 79, 86, 93, 100. *** Dave and Tristle up before first light off the common-room pallets at Holt's and back to the square, where Bircher said Toller would be shifting boxes in the dark, and he is. *** HASK AND DELLIE ARE IN TOWN for this market, logged away from expedition 13 for exactly that. *** THE REST OF THE PARTY IS AT COLL'S BASECAMP with Rowe, the two carts and the mules, and the 101st is the watercourse by the long way round from first light.

*** DAVE AND TRISTLE BACK AT THE BASECAMP BY EVENING, and the party is whole again but for Hask and Dellie, who stay in Wethersby. *** SOLD: ten books and three scrolls to Toller for 27 gp 5 sp -- 26 for the books, 1 gp 5 sp for the scrolls -- which is a thin return on 130 lb carried twenty-two miles and is exactly what he said it would be. 27 xp taken on the price RECEIVED. Purse 1,050 gp 7 sp. *** KEPT: the twenty feet of copper wire, left in Wend's barn with the party's other goods. Toller would not have it -- a smith's business, and he named MUND, who bought their at-cost iron in quantity on the 97th. *** AN ENQUIRY ON THE SET, no offer: the diary, Rogahn's plaque and the headboard, still held on open terms at Toller's own discretion since day 32. *** AT THE BASECAMP MEANWHILE: FRYTHON BEGAN TEACHING BRAND HIS LETTERS (100:2), slow and stubborn, which is the better half of slow. *** TOMORROW IS THE 101st AND THE WATERCOURSE: both carts, the long way round -- Coll's trail down, the fraying road, then the open waste from the road's end -- 6.5 miles instead of the two trackless ones, FROM FIRST LIGHT. Durnhak is owed 196 spikes, 20 lb of nails and the rest of the stores against 75, and the party owes him about 37 gold netted against what it bought for him.

*** DAY 101. THE WATERCOURSE, AND THE CARTS GO THE LONG WAY ROUND FROM FIRST LIGHT, as the player named it on the 99th. *** Spells re-memorised at dawn -- a full night covers the DMG p.40 four-hour minimum, thirty minutes of prayer at first light. Yrtone has back the cure she spent in the library on a single point. *** THE LOAD FOR DURNHAK: 196 iron spikes still owed of the 200 bought off Mund (4 handed over early underground on the 99th), 20 lb of big timber nails, and the rest of the stores against the 75 he named. The party owes him about 37 gold netted against what it bought for him -- ONE TRANSACTION, goods and coin together, which is what Tristle asked for and Durnhak agreed. *** THE ROUTE: 1.8 miles down Coll's graded trail to the crag turning, 1 mile north up the fraying road to the ROAD'S END, then 3.7 miles north-east across open waste to the watercourse mouth. 6.5 miles against the two trackless ones round the north foot. *** THE PARTY HAS RIDDEN THAT WASTE BUT HAS NEVER PUT A WHEEL ON IT.

column3: the open waste, between the road's end and the watercourse
column4: *** GOODBYE TO DURNHAK AND THE THREE RIDE BACK, MEETING THE CART A LITTLE AFTER NOON. *** The horses go back empty -- Durnhak's 232 lb delivered, 28 bars left standing under the overhang because no horse was going to carry eight-foot bar iron out of there today and the cart is what they came for. *** WHERE THINGS STAND, AND IT IS NOT GOOD. The cart went into the waste about eight and has made ABOUT A MILE AND A THIRD IN FOUR HOURS -- roughly three hours a mile, the pace the ground dictates and not the load (d6=2 on what lightening it bought). TWO AND A HALF MILES STILL TO THE WATERCOURSE. At that rate it reaches the overhang about half past seven, AFTER DARK, and then has 588 lb of bar iron to load in it. *** WHAT THE HORSES CHANGE: they are empty now, and they carry 3,000 gp-weight apiece at a normal pace -- 900 lb across the three, against 413 lb of salvage sitting on that cart. THAT IS A FACT AND NOT A SUGGESTION; what the party does with it is the player's. *** NOBODY IS HURT, NOTHING HAS COME AT THEM, and the day's cost so far is entirely hours.

*** THE PARTY SPLITS ON THE WASTE, ABOUT NOON, AND DAVE PUT IT TO THE GROUP BEFORE DECIDING. *** ROWE AND FRYTHON turn the cart around and take it home the easy way -- 1.3 miles back to the road's end (about four hours, the ground being what it is), then 2.8 miles of road and Coll's graded trail. *** ROWE'S POSITION ON DAY 101 WAS NEVER ACTUALLY LOGGED and is settled here rather than assumed: he came north on day 96 treating it as his job and not an adventure, he minds the beasts, and the cart is drawn by a mule. Nothing contradicted it. *** THE OTHER SEVEN WALK TO THE IRON: Dave, Yrtone, Tristle, Torsat, Ista, Blartho and Brand, with the three horses. 2.4 miles out to the watercourse, load, then TWO MILES ROUND THE NORTH FOOT to the basecamp -- the goat line they walked on day 98 in an hour and twenty. *** AND THE SPLIT LEAVES THEM TWO BARS SHORT. Rolled limits: a led horse takes FOUR eight-foot bars before the lashings go (d6=2, bulk not weight), a person takes TWO, one to a shoulder (d6=4). Three horses and seven people is 12 + 14 = TWENTY-SIX. There are TWENTY-EIGHT. *** FRYTHON GOING WITH THE CART IS EXACTLY THE TWO BARS. Not flagged as an objection -- the player was told the per-person limit before he chose -- but the shortfall is real and is the party's to solve. *** THEY DO NOW HAVE A SLAB AND A CUT MARK AT THAT WATERCOURSE, agreed with Durnhak within the hour.

*** THE IRON IS AT THE BASECAMP BY MID-AFTERNOON, CARRIED, AND THE CART COMES HOME EMPTY. *** FRYTHON MOVED ACROSS to the walkers and that closed the arithmetic exactly: eight people at two bars and three horses at four is 28, the whole stack in one lift with nothing spare. *** ROWE TOOK THE CART BACK ALONE (d6=6, no trouble) -- and three things were in his favour that are not the DM being kind: he went back OVER HIS OWN RUTS, which is materially easier than breaking fresh ground; the hard half was behind him at the road's end; and minding beasts is his actual trade. He reached the road about four and was home by dusk. *** THE EIGHT reached the watercourse about twenty to two, loaded in half an hour, and walked the TWO MILES ROUND THE NORTH FOOT to the basecamp by a quarter to four. In daylight. *** THE WHOLE DAY'S LESSON IN ONE LINE: the loop is 6.5 miles and the goat line is 2, and the cart was the reason for taking the long way. Once the iron came off wheels and onto shoulders, the short way was available again.

*** TWENTY-TWO MILES TO WETHERSBY, A FULL DAY, AND NOTHING HAPPENED. *** Out of Coll's basecamp at first light: 2 miles down the graded trail to the crag turning, then 20 miles of made road. One mule and a cart at 7,700 gp-weight -- 17 bars and the whole 413 lb of crag salvage -- three horses at four bars apiece, and everybody walking. *** d6=1: ORDINARY TRAFFIC AND NOTHING THAT STOPPED THEM. The day after market, so carts going home the other way and a good deal of nodding. *** WORTH SAYING PLAINLY BECAUSE THE DICE COULD HAVE SAID OTHERWISE: the party was conspicuous -- 1,022 lb of iron and smith's tools in a hundred where the layoffs are upstream of the robberies, on the road four of its own people used to rob. Nobody took an interest. *** THE BASECAMP IS LEFT EMPTY OF GOODS for the first time since day 96; everything under that lean-to is now in Wethersby. *** ARRIVED AT DUSK. The iron is here, and the man it half belongs to is still owed about 37 gp 5 sp when it sells.

*** CORRECTION TO THE DAY-102 RUN, PLAYER-CAUGHT, AND IT UNWINDS PART OF WHAT I NARRATED. *** The 421 lb of crag salvage and the whole kitchen haul WENT SOUTH WITH HASK AND DELLIE ON THE MORNING OF DAY 99, three days before this cart moved -- availability.tsv says so in Hask's own row: 'one cart, one mule, 421 lb of salvage plus the pans, the sheave block and the kettle. Wethersby by evening.' *** SO THE DAY-102 CART CARRIED IRON AND NOTHING ELSE. 29 bars is 6,090 gp-weight against the 8,000 a mule and cart draw, so ALL TWENTY-NINE FITTED WITH 1,910 TO SPARE and the three horses need not have carried a single bar. My load arithmetic put the cart at 7,700 and split twelve bars onto the horses to make it fit; that was solving a problem that did not exist. *** WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE: the day happened, the journey happened, nothing went wrong on the road, and everything is in Wethersby tonight. THE ERROR WAS IN WHAT THE CART WAS CARRYING, NOT IN WHERE ANYTHING ENDED UP. *** AND THE FILING LESSON IS THE SHARP ONE: a cart's CONTENTS were written into a note about WHO WAS AWAY. inventory_log exists to answer 'where is our stuff' and was never told, so the fact was recorded and unfindable at the same time. L059 closed on it.

Housekeeping in Wethersby: sold daggers and two spears, the load lightened and the strongest bearers repacked, Appendix O weights recorded, two lanterns confirmed (not three) and the second moved from Yrtone to Dave, the town's whole remaining oil stock bought (two flasks), and the holders' 229 gp found already discharged on re-check.
Out of Wethersby at first light: Hask, Dave, Yrtone, Frython, Brand, Tristle, Orm and Rowe, two carts (36 tods of wool, Halm driving) and three horses, south for Ludbury -- five days by cart.

CORRECTION, PLAYER RETCON, same session, added by hand (log.py refused it as behind the already-logged day 108 -- correct, this is a past day, appended anyway per its own instruction). *** TRISTLE DID NOT GO TO LUDBURY. *** The Ludbury party is SEVEN: Hask, Dave, Yrtone, Frython, Brand, Orm and Rowe, plus two carts and three horses. Tristle went instead with Torsat, Blartho, Dellie and Ista to the watercourse, to camp and wait for Durnhak and pay him his 36 gp share of the iron. No dice had depended on his presence in Ludbury when this was caught.

Five days south by cart, three to Marchford and two beyond. One stranger passed on the road near Marchford (d6=3, local traffic, nothing came of it); otherwise ordinary traffic the whole way. Arrived Ludbury with 36 tods of wool, two carts, three horses, and Wend's question about the at-cost rumour still to ask.
CORRECTION, same retcon: the Ludbury party is seven (Hask, Dave, Yrtone, Frython, Brand, Orm, Rowe), not eight. Tristle is at the watercourse, not here.

Dave and Frython, three days east from Ludbury on the light horses. Ordric received them on Neot's name; the free question (what is he learned in) came back Demi-Humankind, not Dweomercraeft -- bad odds and bad money to press him on the ring. Recounted the whole Durnhak story and the crag's history instead; a good hour, nothing further came of it.

Hask, Yrtone, Brand, Orm and Rowe, five days north from Ludbury with two carts and three horses -- they did not wait on Dave and Frython at Wraye. Ordinary traffic the whole way (d6=5). 936 gp from the wool sale and 57 sealed flasks of oil coming home with them.
Dave and Frython back from Wraye, three days. One stranger passed on the road (d6=1, ordinary), nothing came of it. The rest of the party already gone north five days ahead of them.

Yrtone, Hask and Brand out of Wethersby the same day they reported in, seven flasks of oil with them and the rest left in the barn. Orm, Rowe and both carts stay in Wethersby. Word left for Dave and Frython. A day's walk -- crag turning, basecamp, cave mouth, the watercourse -- and they join Tristle, Torsat, Blartho, Dellie and Ista, still camped and still waiting on Durnhak.

Dave and Frython in off the light ride from Ludbury, 2.5 days, nothing further on the road. Find Orm, Rowe and both carts in Wethersby and the word Yrtone's group left: everyone else is at the watercourse, still waiting on Durnhak after ten days with no sign of him.

Dave and Frython in from Wethersby, a day's walk, joining the rest of the party. Ten at the watercourse now (Tristle, Torsat, Blartho, Dellie, Ista, Yrtone, Hask, Brand, Dave, Frython) -- everyone but Orm and Rowe, who stayed with the carts. Ten days camped and no sign of Durnhak.

Off the watercourse by the short way -- the goat line round the north foot, two miles, about an hour and twenty (day 98/101 precedent) -- rather than the scree route. All ten at Coll's basecamp: Tristle, Torsat, Blartho, Dellie, Ista, Yrtone, Hask, Brand, Dave, Frython.

day 118 into 119: rested at Coll's basecamp after expedition 14's first haul out of Quasqueton -- orc gear and the area 11 supplies stored under the lean-to. Frython relearns sleep and continues teaching Brand his letters.

TIME OF DAY, fixed when the player asked and the record had none: expedition 15 began about first light; expedition 16 (rounds 0-966, sixteen hours six minutes, six of them a rest in area 10) began about nine in the morning and ended about ONE O'CLOCK IN THE NIGHT, day 119 into 120. The party walks down to Coll's basecamp in the dark. Out at round 966 alive; Yrtone at 2 of 7 hp out of her coma, to rest a week.

Day 119 into 120: out of Quasqueton at about 1 a.m., down to Coll's basecamp in the dark by about 2, Yrtone cured to 7 of 7 by Blartho's first cure of the night (1d8 = 7), then a full night's rest, eight hours, to about ten in the morning. Blartho re-memorises his cure. YRTONE still owes a week's rest (DMG p.82) after being brought to -8: back about day 126. Expedition 16 ended at round 966; the seven casks became five (a B and a QS left in area 10); the party carries them, with the day's kills' XP banked.

column3: the road south of Coll's basecamp
column4: Day 120: Dave and Tristle rode to the watercourse and back before noon (no answer from Durnhak). About noon the party left the basecamp for Wethersby, 21 miles: Yrtone riding one horse, the loaded horses' cargo split evenly (2,225 and 2,217 gp-wt), the rest on the walkers at 9 inches. About eight miles of the road behind them by dusk; a COLD CAMP by the road, no fire, standard rations. Wethersby is about thirteen miles on, tomorrow.

column3: the road south of Coll's basecamp
column4: CORRECTION to the day-120 travel figures, mine: I said about 8 miles by dusk and 13 to go. From about noon to dusk is roughly 15 miles: so the cold camp is about 15 miles down and about SIX miles short of Wethersby, not thirteen. Still short of Wethersby, as the player said.

Day 121 (a market day: 37 + 7n): a quiet night at the cold camp, the nine watching in turns and Yrtone left to sleep, then the six miles to Wethersby in the morning, arriving about the middle of the morning. Nothing on the road. The party is out of food (all rations eaten, a simplification at the player's word) and Yrtone rides. Yrtone owes a week's rest, back about day 126.

Day 122: up at first light at the Inn, nine of the party (all but Yrtone, resting upstairs on her week) with three carts (the party's two and HALM'S own, he driving), three mules, the three horses and Rowe and Orm, twenty sealed flasks of oil in the carts and the rest of the space empty for the supplies to fetch. Wethersby to Coll's basecamp is 22 miles, a full day for a cart.

Day 122, evening: the three carts (the party's two and Halm's), three mules, three horses, Halm, Orm and Rowe and nine of the party up the road from Wethersby and the two miles of graded trail, at Coll's basecamp about dusk after a full day. Nothing on the road. Blartho has command again. Coll is not there, he only built the camp. Twenty sealed flasks in the carts; the rest of the cart space empty for the supplies.

Day 122, evening, THE TRIP AS IT REALLY WENT AFTER THE UNDO: up at first light at the Inn, nine of the party (all but Yrtone, resting upstairs on her week) with the party's TWO carts and two mules driven by Orm and Rowe, the three horses, and COLL, who walked up the road with them; twenty sealed flasks of oil, 20 person-weeks of raw camp food for the crew and the ten person-weeks of rations, all in the carts. HALM STAYS BEHIND and joins about day 130. Twenty-two miles, a full day; nothing on the road. At Coll's basecamp about dusk. Coll's six hands are due at the camp by day 123.

Coll's six hands come in at first light with picks, shovels, axes and a coil of rope of their own. Coll is ready to walk the outcrop from the camp to the cave mouth with the party and start on the steep pitch the same day (L062). Raw camp food not yet drawn down.

Day 123 ended with dinner (Ista cooking, Dave's step dance in honour of Coll, Torsat, Tristle and Frython keeping the beat) and bed at about half past nine: the lean-to given to the six hands, Orm, Rowe and Coll to split as they can, the party camping out. No wilderness encounters. Sixteen kilderkins, four firkins, two casks, the ropes, saw and sacks are in the lean-to; 33 barrels remain in area 10 (26 sound, 7 slack). Yrtone is at the Inn (fit about day 126); Halm joins about day 130; the sledge-way is in its second working day.

Day 125, first light at Coll's basecamp after a quiet night. Day 124 ended with Tristle's ballet for Coll (Dave and Torsat humming, somber and then silly) and bed at about nine: the lean-to to Coll and the hands, the party outside. No wilderness encounters. The party's gear is in the lean-to. Hask caught Rowe and Orm on the road about 2:20 pm and told them to bring back all the oil from Wend's barn (27 sealed flasks); they were to reach Wethersby about dusk on day 124, unload eleven kilderkins and a firkin at the barn, and are due back at the basecamp at dusk on day 125 (loop L063). Coll's sledge-way is in its third working day and stands about the morning of day 129. Yrtone at the Inn, fit about day 126; Halm joins about day 130.

Day 126, first light at Coll's basecamp after a quiet night; the party works the day with Coll, gear off in the lean-to. Day 125 ended with dinner, Ferd's and Wat's dances, and Dave's ask: Coll agreed the crew will haul barrels down the sledge-way on the days the road saves (loop L064), the outcrop only, never into the caves. Dave told Coll the party would help again on day 126 and go into the caves on day 127 to start bringing barrels out. The sledge-way stands early afternoon on day 126 (about 52.75 of 49 man-days). Yrtone is fit from today at the Inn. Halm joins about day 130.

Day 127, first light at the cave mouth after a night of watches over the twenty-seven barrels and kilderkins standing there. Day 126 ended with three more barrel trips out of area 10 (every container of the day-119 census is out of the storeroom), the crew's sledges running until dark (six barrels below), dinner at the basecamp, and two berserkers coming down the corridor at about 10:30 pm and shot dead in the first surprise segment by Dave and Torsat on watch (XP 29). Their bodies and arrows lie in the corridor, unsearched. The rest of the night quiet. Dave asked Coll for two improvised sledges from green poles: two by mid-morning, four men to each. Yrtone walks from Wethersby and reaches the basecamp about midday. Halm joins about day 130.

Day 128, first light at Coll's basecamp after a quiet night. Day 127 ended with the last barrels sledged down the outcrop in the dark, Dave's thanks (a gold piece each to six hands, Rowe and Orm and two to Coll, ten from the purse) and dancing. Morning: two carts and three horses loaded from the lean-to with the containers they can carry (about 29,700 gp-wt: LC, HU, VW / MK, B, TL, cask B / B, XR / Z, QS / OG, HU firkin) and sent to Wend's barn with the party but Dave, Tristle and Yrtone, and Coll's crew going home to Wethersby; 22 miles, a full day, dusk. The trio walk the goat line to the watercourse and back. Thirty containers remain in the lean-to with the oil (23 flasks) and the camp food (7.39 person-weeks). Halm joins at Wethersby about day 130.

Day 129, first light at the Inn at Wethersby after a quiet night. Day 128: the caravan reached Wethersby about dusk and left thirteen containers (LC, HU, MK, B, B, OG, QS barrels; the XR and Z kilderkins; firkins VW, TL and HU; cask B) at Wend's barn; the seven of the party who went with it (Torsat, Blartho, Frython, Hask, Dellie, Ista, Brand) spent the night at the Inn two to a room, and Dave, Tristle and Yrtone walked the 21 miles through the day and joined them about half past ten. Coll and his hands went home; Rowe and Orm stabled the animals. Thirty containers, the oil, the camp food and the four sledges are at the basecamp. Halm is due about day 130. Ten of the party present.

Day 130, first light at Coll's basecamp after a quiet night. The caravan and the trio spent the night together at the lean-to. Morning: the two carts and three horses loaded with what they can carry (about 30,000 gp-wt: B, TL, cask QS, Y / PF, UT / Z kilderkin, QS / LC / SD kilderkin, HU, and the sealed oil, ropes, sacks and crosscut saw), everyone on foot with the animals, to Wend's barn, 21 miles, in by late afternoon. Nineteen containers, the four sledges and the camp food remain at the basecamp. HALM IS NOT ON THE ROAD: d6 = 4, Wend has not put it to him (loop L061). Ten of the party present.

Day 131: up at the Inn, Wend wrote Halm's hire down at the barn at first light (8 sp a day, owed on his return), and three carts (Halm's, the party's two), three mules, three horses, Rowe, Orm and the ten of the party set out for the basecamp, 21 miles, a full day; nothing on the road; at the basecamp about dusk; a night at the lean-to.

Day 132: loaded at the basecamp at first light with what the three carts and three horses can carry (eleven containers, about 33,300 gp-wt: B and the SD barrel, AW and TL, FT, RH and Y, the SD kilderkin and JS, OG, LC), everyone on foot with the animals, and Wethersby by dusk; unloaded at Wend's barn. Eight barrels remain at the basecamp (AW, EJ, GG, TL, UT, VW, Z, Z), with the four sledges and the last camp food. HALM'S HIRE IS OWED: two days at 8 sp, 16 sp, on his return; not paid yet. Ten of the party present.

Day 133: Halm paid for the first run (16 sp, booked to Halm, not Coll; the player named Coll by a slip and Coll is owed nothing), a night at the Inn (ten gold pieces), then the party, Rowe, Orm and Halm with three carts, mules and three horses out at first light for the last load, 21 miles, at the basecamp about dusk; a night at the lean-to. Nothing on the road.

Day 134: the last load. Loaded at first light at the basecamp by the most that will go: a Z barrel on each of Halm's cart and cart 1, AW and GG on cart 2, EJ, UT and VW on the three horses (seven of the eight barrels; the smallest, TL, has no room left on any carrier and stays with the four sledges and the last of the camp food). At Wend's barn by dusk. HALM IS OWED another 16 sp for days 133 and 134. Ten of the party present.

Rowe with one cart and one mule and Yrtone, Torsat, Blartho, Hask, Dellie, Ista and Brand set out for the basecamp to load the last barrel (TL) with the five days of camp food bought yesterday (5.71 person-weeks) and all the oil that was at the barn, which they will leave in the lean-to at the party's word; at the basecamp about dusk; they use up the 1.67 person-weeks there. Dave, Tristle and Frython stay in Wethersby to talk to Holt at Wend's barn after the morning rush. Halm is owed 16 sp for days 133 and 134, unpaid.

Day 136 in Wethersby. Night at the Inn on Holt's tab (the trio; first tab rows on day 135). Frython spends the day in Toller's shop with the area 6 papers and the journal, now that every barrel mark is decoded (L050 and L011): d100 = 18 against 90, SUCCESS. The eight (Rowe, Yrtone, Torsat, Blartho, Hask, Dellie, Ista, Brand with the cart and the last TL barrel) are due at dusk. Halm paid; Osk's cart hire accepted; the offscreen agendas are running.

Day 137: a night at the Inn on Holt's tab (ten of the party; two of the three hacksaws left at Wend's barn first). In the morning the party sold the silver mirror to Toller (90 gp), bought lunch for the road (ten merchant's meals) and set out north about half past nine for the basecamp, all ten, with the three horses (the shared kit on them), 21 miles; at the basecamp about dusk; dinner from the camp food. Nothing on the road. Purpose: the trip back up.

Day 138, first light at Coll's basecamp after a quiet night at the lean-to. Day 137 ended with the trio at the slab (Durnhak has answered: a meeting at the watercourse at noon on day 139, bring the 36 gp) and the party's working purse of a hundred gold carried as weight. Morning: breakfast, up the sledge-way to the cave mouth (half an hour at 9 inches), in in standard formation, Tristle 40 ft ahead, everyone with a missile weapon ready, to the corridor at the mouth of area 22. The three horses stay at the basecamp.

Day 139, first light at Coll's basecamp after a quiet night: bed about 9 pm after Brand's harvest dance and the party's cheering, no watch kept and nothing on the road. Eight empty barrels from area 13 stacked under the lean-to, the four sledges at the camp; the orc arms, eight mallets and the box of pegs left there. Today: noon at the watercourse with Durnhak and the 36 gp.

The long sword, the barbarian sword and the orc spear, and the carried camp food, all left at the basecamp. Yesterday closed level 2's first ground: both troglodytes and the black widow spider of the western cavern dead, four small gold rods recovered, and a partnership opened with Durnhak's people for the deeper workings (L067).

Day 141, first light at Coll's basecamp after a quiet night, no watch incident. Loading the cart for the trip into Wethersby: mallets, empty barrels (stacked and roped down), spears, the orc polearm, the long sword and barbarian sword, the box of pegs, and the salvage weapons brought up from the dungeon (military picks, short swords, javelins, spare slings); camp food packed for the lunch stop.

Day 142, first light at the Inn in Wethersby after a quiet night. Yrtone, healed and rested, re-memorises her spells with detect magic in place of command -- first use: the barbarian sword from area 39. Buying three days of standard rations and camp food for the party, then to Wend's barn for more iron spikes, dropping off the ore sample and the spare slings.
